land.text: Ruanda and Urundi, the two districts of former German East Africa

predecessors.note: Ceded to Belgium under the Anglo-Belgian agreement of 30 May 1919; the kingdoms of Rwanda and Burundi survived under German and Belgian rule (dossiers kingdom-of-rwanda and kingdom-of-burundi).

successors.note: 'broken up along traditional lines as the independent Republic of Rwanda and Kingdom of Burundi'; the Rwandan monarchy was abolished in September 1961.

correction.text: Ruanda and Urundi, the two districts of former German East Africa

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; the lands sit in its Belgian Congo aggregate or German Africa). 'Ruanda was occupied over April-May and Urundi in June 1916'; infobox 'Belgian occupation: 6 May 1916'. The page gives no area; Rwanda and Burundi resolve to about 46,000 km2 in the gazetteer. By September 1916 the Belgians also held Kigoma, Karema and Tabora ('a large portion of German East Africa'), which Smuts later ordered them to leave; that wider zone is not drawn (see notes).

ledger.note: 1916 (6 May): Belgian forces occupy Ruanda. Infobox 'Belgian occupation: 6 May 1916'; 'Ruanda was occupied over April-May and Urundi in June 1916'; the East African campaign page: the Force Publique 'captured Kigali in Rwanda on 6 May'.

region.text: Ruanda and Urundi, the two districts of former German East Africa

ledger.note: 1916 (6 May): the Force Publique takes Kigali and the Belgians move through Ruanda ('captured Kigali in Rwanda on 6 May'; the Belgians held Ruanda and Urundi by 17 June).
1916 (June): Belgian forces occupy Urundi. 'Ruanda was occupied over April-May and Urundi in June 1916'.

region.text: Ruanda and Urundi, the two districts of former German East Africa

ledger.note: 1916 (June): both districts are in Belgian hands. 'The Belgian Force Publique occupied Rwanda and Burundi by 17 June 1916'; later Smuts ordered the Belgians back to the Congo, leaving them in Rwanda and Burundi only.

1919 (30 May): Britain cedes Ruanda and Urundi to Belgium. 'Britain ceded the north-western GEA districts of Ruanda and Urundi to Belgium' in the Anglo-Belgian agreement of 30 May 1919, confirmed by the Treaty of Versailles (28 June 1919).

1922 (20 July): the League of Nations makes Ruanda-Urundi a Belgian mandate. 'the League of Nations officially awarded Ruanda-Urundi to Belgium as a B-Class Mandate on 20 July 1922'; on 1 March 1926 it was administratively merged with the Belgian Congo.

1946 (13 December): the mandate becomes a UN Trust Territory. The UN 'voted to end the mandate over Ruanda-Urundi and replace it with the new status of Trust Territory'; infobox '13 December 1946'. Rwanda gained autonomy on 18 October 1960 and Burundi on 21 December 1961.

region.text: Ruanda and Urundi, the two districts of former German East Africa

ledger.note: 1962 (1 July): Ruanda-Urundi splits into two independent states. 'Ruanda-Urundi became independent on 1 July 1962, broken up along traditional lines as the independent Republic of Rwanda and Kingdom of Burundi.'

wars.name: East African campaign (World War I)

zones.text: Ruanda and Urundi, the two districts of former German East Africa

wars.outcome: Belgian occupation of Ruanda (April-May 1916) and Urundi (June 1916); the Anglo-Belgian agreement of 30 May 1919 gave the districts to Belgium.
wars.note: Only the Belgian share of the campaign (1916) falls in this state's life; the whole war ran 3 August 1914 to 25 November 1918.

certainty.note: The frontiers with the Belgian Congo, Tanganyika and Uganda are not on any page opened; they follow the districts of the German East Africa years (the Kivu-Mfumbiro boundary is not covered).

notes:
A small state of two districts, written from three pages (the Ruanda-Urundi article gives no area). The wider Belgian occupation of September 1916 (Kigoma, Karema, Tabora: 'a large portion of German East Africa') is not drawn: Smuts ordered the Belgians back to the Congo, and the pages opened date neither the withdrawal nor the Belgian handing over of Tabora; a gap-filler could add an occupation event for the German East Africa lands (counterpart german-east-africa) from the East African campaign article.
The `rename` events mark status changes of the same state (occupation, cession of 1919, B mandate of 1922, trust of 1946). The administrative union with the Belgian Congo of 1 March 1926 is not a change of land and has no event. Successors: the Cliopatria rows republic-of-rwanda and republic-of-burundi both start in 1963 (polities.csv), so the dossier's end year of 1962 leaves one empty year on the map. The kings and the Tutsi-Hutu revolution of 1959-61 are for the Kingdom of Rwanda and Kingdom of Burundi dossiers.
